findings.evidence: "This recommendation removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification." The grounds behind it are one twelve-month pilot at four of the consortium's ten branches, measured by an avoidance survey and an uncorroborated return-rate claim.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim to match its evidence, for example end overdue fines at all ten branches starting next fiscal year, subject to review after the first year, rather than permanently and without qualification.
findings.violation: The claim is asserted with maximal, unqualified certainty (permanently, every item, without qualification) while the only evidence behind it is a single twelve-month pilot at four of ten branches, so a decision-maker reading the Recommendation section alone gets no signal that the result might not generalize to the six untested branches or to every item type, or that it might need revisiting.

findings.evidence: First paragraph: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year." Second paragraph, immediately after: "Specifically, the recommended change is about making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable."
findings.fix: Delete the "in whatever way the consortium finds workable" sentence, or replace it with a restatement that repeats the same ten-branch, next-fiscal-year scope rather than loosening it.
findings.violation: The specific, falsifiable ask stated in the first paragraph is immediately dissolved into a vacuous restatement that names no policy, no scope, and no date, so a reader cannot tell whether the ask is the ten-branch fine elimination just stated or an open-ended commitment to whatever the consortium later finds workable.

findings.evidence: Addressing the Revenue Concern raises and answers the lost-revenue objection with finance data. Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide asserts generalization from the four piloted branches to all ten through a general principle and an outside citation, without naming any way the six branches that were never piloted could differ from the four that were.
findings.fix: Add a passage naming the branch-to-branch differences, such as size, patron base, or reliance on fine revenue, that could make the other six branches behave differently from the pilot four, and explain why the consortium should expect the result to hold anyway.
findings.location: ## Addressing the Revenue Concern; ## Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide
findings.violation: The artifact raises and answers one foreseeable objection, lost revenue, but never raises the second foreseeable one its own scope invites: the pilot covered only four of the consortium's ten branches, and nothing in the document considers what might differ at the six branches extending the policy covers but never tested.
